# Contribute {#contribute}

This wiki is intended to be added to. If you have a worked example, a repository
comparison, a language-specific pitfall, or a correction, this page explains how
to get it in.

::: {.tada-key}
Copy [`templates/page-template.Rmd`](templates/page-template.Rmd), fill it in,
add the filename to `_bookdown.yml`, run `Rscript render.R`, and open a pull
request. The rest of this page is detail.
:::

## What belongs here {#contribute-scope}

**Yes, please:**

- Worked examples: a real README, a real project structure, a real code review
- Language- or tool-specific guidance (Julia, MATLAB, Stata, Snakemake…)
- Discipline-specific notes. TADA was developed in ecology and evolutionary
  biology, and the authors explicitly encourage adaptation to other fields
- Repository, licence or journal-policy information that has changed
- Corrections, especially anywhere this wiki has drifted from the source papers

**Probably not:**

- General programming tutorials. Link to them from
  [Further reading](#further-reading) instead
- Advocacy for a particular statistical method
- Tool recommendations with no connection to sharing, archiving or review

## Sourcing {#contribute-sourcing}

::: {.tada-warn}
**Separate what the papers say from what you are adding.**

If a claim comes from one of the three source papers, state that and cite it, by
author and year, so that a reader can find it in [References](#references). If
it is your own practical advice, label it **wiki guidance**, as this wiki does
throughout.

This separation is what makes the wiki usable. A page that blends sourced
findings with the contributor's own advice leaves a reader unable to tell which
is which.
:::

Concretely:

> The SORTEE guidelines require that code files are in an interoperable format
> (Guideline 3.4). ✅ *sourced, and pinpointed*
>
> Wiki guidance: in practice, the quickest way to check this is to open every
> file in a plain text editor before you deposit. ✅ *labelled as an addition*
>
> You must always use `.csv` for data. ❌ *unsourced, and stronger than the
> source*

## File layout {#contribute-layout}

```
TADA-Wiki/
├── index.Rmd              Welcome page (chapter order lives in _bookdown.yml)
├── 01-quickstart.Rmd      … one file per chapter, numbered in reading order
├── 11-references.Rmd
├── _bookdown.yml          Chapter list, output directory, labels
├── _output.yml            Theme, CSS, includes, repository links
├── render.R               Build script
├── assets/
│   ├── style.css          All styling. Design tokens at the top; light theme only
│   ├── tada.js            Turns `.tabset` sections into tabs
│   ├── head.html          Injected into <head> of every page
│   └── foot.html          Injected at the end of <body> of every page
├── templates/             Copy-and-fill templates for readers
├── papers/                The three source PDFs
└── docs/                  Rendered site — generated, do not edit by hand
```

## Adding a chapter {#contribute-chapter}

1. **Copy the template.**

   ```bash
   cp templates/page-template.Rmd 12-my-new-chapter.Rmd
   ```

2. **Give it a heading and an ID.** Every chapter starts with a level-1 heading
   carrying an explicit ID, because other pages link to it:

   ```markdown
   # My new chapter {#my-new-chapter}
   ```

3. **Register it** in `_bookdown.yml`, in the position you want it to appear:

   ```yaml
   rmd_files:
     - "index.Rmd"
     ...
     - "12-my-new-chapter.Rmd"
     - "11-references.Rmd"   # keep references last
   ```

4. **Build and check.**

   ```bash
   Rscript render.R
   ```

   Open `docs/index.html`.

::: {.tada-warn}
**Nothing validates your links.** A broken `](#some-id)` cross-reference does
not fail the build, or even warn: it renders as a dead link and the build still
exits successfully. Check new links by hand in `docs/`, or grep the built site
for the anchor you expect.
:::

## Writing conventions {#contribute-style}

### Cross-references {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Link by ID: `[Transferable](#transferable)`, `[the four Rs](#review-four-rs)`.
Give every section you might want to link to an explicit `{#id}`, because
auto-generated IDs change when you edit a heading and silently break links.

### Callouts {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Four are defined in `assets/style.css`. Use them sparingly, since callouts lose
their effect if most of a page sits inside one.

```markdown
::: {.tada-key}
The short version — one paragraph that summarises the section.
:::

::: {.tada-tip}
Try this — a concrete, actionable suggestion.
:::

::: {.tada-warn}
Watch out — a common, costly mistake.
:::

::: {.tada-note}
Note — a caveat, exception, or aside.
:::
```

### Tabs {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Wrap the panes in a `.tabset` div. Each heading inside becomes a tab label, so
mark them `{.unlisted .unnumbered}` to keep them out of the contents listing and
out of the section numbering.

```markdown
::: {.tabset}

#### R {.unlisted .unnumbered}

...

#### Python {.unlisted .unnumbered}

...

:::
```

`assets/tada.js` finds any element with the `tabset` class, so putting
`{.tabset}` on a heading instead (`## How to do it {#some-id .tabset}`) also
works. Use the div form in chapters, because it makes the extent of the tab
group explicit.

With JavaScript disabled every pane renders in sequence, so never put anything
in a tab that the page depends on being hidden.

### Before / after code {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Use `::::` for the outer fence. Pandoc nests same-width fences correctly either
way, but the wider outer fence makes the grouping obvious to the next person
editing the file.

````markdown
:::: {.tada-compare}
::: {.tada-before}
Before

```r
setwd("C:/Users/me/project")
```
:::

::: {.tada-after}
After

```r
library(here)
```
:::
::::
````

### Checklists {.unlisted .unnumbered}

End substantial chapters with one. Markdown task syntax, one item per line:

```markdown
- [ ] Something the reader can verify in under a minute
```

Keep every item in the same grammatical form: a declarative statement of the
finished state, not a mixture of imperatives and noun phrases.

### Code chunks {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Chunks are set to `eval = FALSE` globally in `index.Rmd`, because code on this
wiki is illustrative and is never executed at build time. If you genuinely need
a chunk to run, set `eval = TRUE` on that chunk *and* state the dependency in
your pull request, because it becomes a build requirement for everyone.

To show an R chunk *as an example* inside a fenced block, use knitr's verbatim
engine, as [Annotated](#annotated-literate) does. Without it, knitr finds the
inner chunk header and executes it, and the header vanishes from the rendered
page:

````markdown
````{verbatim, lang="markdown"}
```{r example-chunk}
1 + 1
```
````
````

### Voice {.unlisted .unnumbered}

- Second person, present tense. "Save your code as `.R`", not "code should be
  saved".
- State the guideline, then give the reason for it. The reason is what makes it
  memorable.
- Prefer concrete numbers to adjectives. "74% of archived R files failed to run"
  beats "many files fail to run".
- Assume the reader is a competent researcher who has never archived code
  before, rather than a novice programmer or a software engineer.
- British spelling throughout (*licence* as the noun, *license* as the verb;
  *organise*, *analyse*). Direct quotations from the source papers keep their
  original spelling.

## References {#contribute-references}

Add new sources to `11-references.Rmd`, alphabetically by first author, in the
existing format:

```markdown
**Author, A. B., & Author, C. D.** (Year). *Title of the work.* Journal
Volume: pages. <https://doi.org/…>
```

Include a DOI wherever one exists. If you cite something in a chapter, it must
appear in that list.

## Submitting {#contribute-submitting}

To propose a change:

```bash
git checkout -b add-julia-guidance
git add 12-julia.Rmd _bookdown.yml 11-references.Rmd
git commit -m "Add Julia-specific transferability guidance"
git push -u origin add-julia-guidance
```

Then open a pull request describing **what you added** and **where it came
from**, whether sourced from a paper or from your own practice.

::: {.tada-note}
For small corrections, the **Edit this page** link in the footer of every
chapter is quicker: it opens the source `.Rmd` on GitHub, ready to edit.
:::

### Before you submit {.unlisted .unnumbered}

- [ ] `Rscript render.R` completes without errors
- [ ] Every claim from a source paper is attributed, and every addition of your own is labelled as wiki guidance
- [ ] New sources are in `11-references.Rmd`
- [ ] Every heading you link to has an explicit `{#id}`
- [ ] Cross-references resolve when clicked in `docs/`
- [ ] The chapter is registered in `_bookdown.yml`
- [ ] The page has been checked at a narrow window width
- [ ] `docs/` changes are either included in the commit or excluded consistently, and the pull request says which
